newsitem.title: USA: Eagle Finance sees Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Eagle Finance sees Q1 loss.

text.p: Eagle Finance Corp, a specialized financial services company that purchases and services installment contracts, said Monday it expects to report a loss for the first quarter.
Eagle Finance today reported a loss of $1.38 a share for the 1996 fourth quarter.
In the year-ago first quarter Eagle Finance reported net income of $0.02 a share.
Commenting on its expected loss for the 1997 first quarter, it said purchases of new finance receivables are expected to remain at low levels due to changes instituted to improve credit quality.
It said it had received waivers from it lenders for covenant violations due to the anticipated first quarter loss.
Eagle also several programs are now in place that are intended to reduce operating expenses.

Eagle Finance said its 1996 results were hurt by higher loan loss provisions, operating expenses and funding decisions. It said it had received waivers from its lenders with respect to convenant violations due to the fourth quarter and full-year 1996 losses.
The company recognized a $6.6 million provision for credit losses in the fourth quarter, resulting in a total provision of $13.2 million in 1996.
Net charges-offs were 19.6 percent of average net managed auto receivables in 1996, compared with 15.6 percent in 1995.
During 1996, owned receivables declined $91 million, due in part to the sale of about $100 million of finance receivables.
Managed receivables as of December 31 were down $33.3 million from a year earlier, to $151.6 million, but serviced finance receivables increased $57.8 million, to $97.0 million.

Eagle Finance said it exited several markets in 1996, refocusing on the midwestern and southeastern United States. In the fourth quarter it began implementing a credit scoring program. It also established a formal risk management function and tightened controls over both underwriting and collections.
